validity.researcher_notes:
EXISTENCE: solidly confirmed, independent of GEM. FERC has an active administrative record for this exact operator entity spanning 17 years: pre-filing NOI docket PF09-9-000 (Fed. Reg. 2009-05-26, E9-12075), the construction certificate application (CP09-460, cited in NaturalGasIntel 2010-01-27), the EA-availability notice (Fed. Reg. 2010-02-02, 2010-2108), and -- critically -- ETC Tiger Pipeline, LLC is STILL an active FERC applicant as of 2026: Docket CP26-549 (Fed. Reg. 2026-07-21 + follow-up scoping notice 2026-08-28) is that same entity's new 'Franklin Farms Project' filing, giving Houston address 1300 Main Street and an @energytransfer.com contact. Trade press (NaturalGasIntel 2010 and 2011, Oil & Gas Journal, Hydrocarbons Technology) all independently describe the same physical pipeline (Carthage TX Panola County interconnect with Houston Pipe Line -> Perryville Hub/Delhi, Richland Parish LA, 42-inch, ~175 mi). Not a phantom or GEM-only entity.

CLASSIFICATION: correct. NGA Section 7(c)-jurisdictional INTERSTATE natural gas TRANSMISSION pipeline per FERC dockets and every trade-press source; Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission both confirmed.

DUPLICATE CHECK (against the 45-row roster + adjacent PIDs): NOT a duplicate. No other roster row covers this Carthage-Delhi trunk. But GEM does carry a SIBLING row for this same pipeline family, P5849 ('Tiger Gas Pipeline', both endpoints in Louisiana, 21 mi, 42in, 400 MMcf/d, $193,000,000 USD, StartYear1=2011) that is correctly excluded from this Texas-scoped batch. That row is the 2011 looping expansion -- 20.5 mi of new 42-in loop + 30,565 hp added compression, cost $193M, confirmed via NaturalGasIntel's 2011-07-21 'FERC Clears ETC Tiger Pipeline Expansion for Service' and Oil & Gas Journal's 'Energy Transfer Partners expands Tiger Pipeline' -- both independent of GEM. Mainline (P0265: 175 mi / 2,000 MMcf/d, 2010) + loop (P5849: 21 mi / 400 MMcf/d, 2011) sum to ~196 mi and 2,400 MMcf/d, matching every source's description of the pipeline's current (post-2011) totals (Hydrocarbons Technology: 'extended by 20 miles in August 2011...total capacity...2.4bcf per day'). This is the correct segment-vs-network split, not a double count -- flagging the cross-reference for the record only, no action needed. Also confirmed 'ETP Legacy' is a real, consistently-applied GEM owner tag: it appears on 10 rows tracker-wide including P5849, not a one-off typo.

ATTRIBUTION: Operator 'ETC Tiger Pipeline LLC' confirmed -- exact legal-entity name in FERC's own Federal Register notices (2009 through 2026) and in Energy Transfer Partners LP's FY2009 Form 10-K ('ETC Tiger Pipeline, LLC ("ETC Tiger")'), and in NaturalGasIntel ('Tiger Pipeline Co. LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary of Energy Transfer Partners LP'). Owner 'ETP Legacy' / 100% confirmed -- ETP's own 10-K consolidates ETC Tiger as a wholly-owned subsidiary, and the entity remains part of the Energy Transfer family as of the 2026 FERC filing.

SPEC, checked individually against >=2 independent sources each: Length 175 mi -- HIGH (NaturalGasIntel 2010: '175-mile, 42-inch diameter pipeline'; NaturalGasIntel 2011 FERC-clears article: 'a 175-mile pipeline'; Hydrocarbons Technology: 'initially 175 miles'). Diameter 42 in -- HIGH (same three sources plus OGJ: '42-in. Tiger gas pipeline'). Capacity 2,000 MMcf/d -- HIGH and correctly the MAINLINE-ONLY figure: NaturalGasIntel 2010 ('capacity to transport up to 2 Bcf/d') and Hydrocarbons Technology ('initial capacity to transport two billion cubic feet (bcf) of natural gas per day') both independently give 2 Bcf/d as the ORIGINAL design capacity, before the +400 MMcf/d 2011 loop that GEM tracks separately on P5849 -- so GEM is not stale here, it is correctly segmented. ConstructionYear/Month 2010-06 -- HIGH (Hydrocarbons Technology: 'Construction Start June 2010'; corroborated by the FERC construction-authorization timing referenced in the same source). StartYear1 2010 -- HIGH: NaturalGasIntel's 2011-07-21 article states the original mainline, 'most of which went into operation in December[2010]' (bracket mine, from context: it cites a 2010-11-09 Daily GPI story as background), and Hydrocarbons Technology's body text says 'it became operational in December 2010' -- note that same source's own info-box display has an internal typo ('Completion December 2011') that contradicts its own body text; the two independent NGI articles resolve the discrepancy in favor of December 2010, matching GEM. Location (Carthage, TX -> Delhi, LA) -- HIGH: ETP's own FY2009 10-K independently names the terminus 'end near Delhi, Louisiana,' matching GEM's EndLocation exactly, and Hydrocarbons Technology separately confirms 'laid from Catharage [sic] in East Texas to Delhi in Louisiana.' SegmentCost $1,200,000,000 USD -- the figure is confirmed CORRECT (ETP's FY2009 Form 10-K states verbatim: 'We expect the total costs of this project to be $1.2 billion, excluding the costs of the recently announced expansion'), but I could NOT get a url_verifier-passing citation for it: SEC.gov returns HTTP 403 to the verifier's default UA (confirmed with a browser-like UA that the page is live and genuine, not a dead link -- this is the documented SEC bot-wall false-negative family, not evidence of deletion). Per the hard rule I did not stage an unverified URL; recommend a follow-up with a Wayback capture of https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001012569/000119312510039066/d10k.htm (IA's availability API was itself rate-limited, HTTP 429, when I tried).

HARVESTED CITATION POOL (wiki_citations.json, 6 entries): opened/screened all 6. bit.ly/2sYGqrY resolves to abarrelfull.wikidot.com -- BANNED, correctly excluded from all outputs. https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php is a generic data-portal landing page (navigation surface, does not name this pipeline) -- not cited, consistent with the egyptoil-gas.com rule. casetext.com/federal-register/etc-tiger-pipeline-llc-notice-of-application -- HTTP 410 Gone (page genuinely removed; recovered the same underlying Federal Register document directly at federalregister.gov instead, which is live and citable). ir.energytransfer.com's two press releases (open season announcement, Feb 2009) both ReadTimeout on repeated tries -- an access failure, not a deletion; not cited, no action taken since the same fact (Chesapeake/EnCana open-season commitments) is independently confirmed by ETP's own 10-K and NaturalGasIntel. naturalgasintel.com/.../energy-transfer-tiger-pipeline-gets-environmental-nod/ and hydrocarbons-technology.com/projects/etctigerpipelineproj/ both opened successfully and are cited above. Additionally found and verified (outside the harvested pool, via targeted search) two more NaturalGasIntel articles, one Oil & Gas Journal article, and four FERC Federal Register notices (2009, 2010, and two from 2026) -- all cited above.

DISCOVERY LEAD (out of scope for this validity pass, flagged for the record): FERC Docket CP26-549, filed 2026-07-01 and still in EA scoping as of 2026-08-28, is ETC Tiger Pipeline LLC's proposed 'Franklin Farms Project' -- ~13.24 mi of NEW 36-in greenfield lateral plus ~1.75 mi of 20-in lateral in Richland Parish, LA ($137,388,622 estimated cost), to deliver ~1,000,000 Dth/d to Entergy Louisiana's Richland Parish Data Center power-generation facility, interconnecting with MEP, Gulf South, Gulf Crossing, and Gulf Run pipelines. Checked against the full 45-row roster plus P5849/P5823 -- this is not yet tracked anywhere in GEM under any PID I could find. It is pre-FID, in Louisiana (out of this batch's Texas scope), and a genuinely new facility rather than a data point on P0265, so I am not staging it here -- routing it to a future Louisiana/Discovery pass instead.

summary: P0265 (Tiger Gas Pipeline mainline, Carthage TX -> Delhi LA) confirmed real, correctly classified, correctly attributed, and correct on all spec fields (175mi/42in/2,000 MMcf/d/2010) against 4+ independent trade-press and FERC sources; verdict=confirmed (caveat), concern_type=none. Sibling P5849 is the 2011 expansion loop, correctly segmented not duplicated. One item left UNRESOLVED for ref purposes: SegmentCost $1.2B is confirmed correct via ETP's FY2009 10-K but SEC.gov 403s url_verifier's UA so no citable URL was staged.
